title: A Camera Shot 10 Trillion Frames a Second to Film a Laser

scenes.text: Scientists built a camera that shoots ten trillion frames a second.
In 2018, teams in Quebec and at Caltech used it to film a laser pulse in real time.
The pulse lasted femtoseconds, millionths of a billionth of a second.
The camera caught it in twenty five frames.
Twenty five frames of a flash too fast to ever see.

description:
A camera called T-CUP can shoot ten trillion frames per second.
In 2018, researchers at INRS in Quebec and Caltech used it to record a femtosecond laser pulse in 25 frames.
What would you film with a camera like this? Comment below.
first_comment: This camera filmed a laser pulse. What would you want to see in slow motion?
